title: Unit 8: Applications of Integration

topics.name: Average value and accumulation in context
covers: Determining the average value of a function using definite integrals

topics.name: Area and volume
covers: Determining volume with cross-sections, the disc method, and the washer method

guide.title: Applications of integration: review guide
guide.intro: Definite integrals find totals: average values, distances, amounts in a tank, areas, and volumes. Most problems come down to setting up the right integrand and limits.

sections.title: Average value and accumulation
body: The average value of f on [a, b] is the integral divided by the interval length. For an amount, start with the initial value and add the integral of the net rate (in minus out).
equations: A(t) = A(0) + ∫₀ᵗ (rate in − rate out) dx

sections.title: Motion
body: Displacement is ∫ v(t) dt, which can be negative. Total distance is ∫ |v(t)| dt: split the interval where v changes sign.

sections.title: Area and volume
body: Area between curves is ∫ (top − bottom) dx, or ∫ (right − left) dy when integrating along y. For volume, integrate the area of a cross-section.
points: Discs: π∫ R² dx. Washers: π∫ (R² − r²) dx, subtracting squares, not squaring the difference.
Known cross-sections: square with side s has area s². Semicircle with diameter s has area (π/8)s².
Find intersection points first to get the limits.

example.prompt: A particle has v(t) = t² − 4 m/s for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3. Find its total distance traveled.
example.solution: v changes sign at t = 2. Distance = ∫₀² (4 − t²) dt + ∫₂³ (t² − 4) dt = 16/3 + 7/3 = 23/3 ≈ 7.67 m. Its displacement would be −16/3 + 7/3 = −3 m.

misconceptions: Distance adds the absolute values, so parts where v < 0 count positively.
“The average value is the average of the endpoint values.”
Use the integral divided by the interval length.

questions.prompt: What is the average value of f(x) = x² on [0, 3]?
choiceExplanations: 4.5 averages the endpoint values f(0) and f(3). That is not the average value of the function.
9 is the integral itself. Divide by the interval length, 3.
2.25 is f at the midpoint, f(1.5). That is not the average value in general.

questions.prompt: What is the area of the region between y = x and y = x² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1?
questions.explanation: On [0, 1], x ≥ x², so the area is ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6.
choiceExplanations: This subtracts top from bottom. Area uses top − bottom, so it is positive.
5/6 adds the two integrals instead of subtracting.
1/2 is the area under y = x alone.

questions.prompt: A particle moves with velocity v(t) = 3t² m/s and is at position 2 m at t = 0. What is its position at t = 2?
choiceExplanations: 12 is v(2), the velocity at t = 2, not a position.
14 adds the starting position to v(2). Add the integral of v instead.
8 is the displacement. Add the starting position of 2 m.

questions.prompt: A particle has velocity v(t) = t − 2 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. What is its total distance traveled?
questions.explanation: v < 0 on [0, 2] and v > 0 on [2, 4]. Distance = ∫₀² (2 − t) dt + ∫₂⁴ (t − 2) dt = 2 + 2 = 4.
choiceExplanations: 8 is ∫₀⁴ t dt, which leaves out the −2 in the velocity.
2 counts only one of the two parts of the motion.
0 is the displacement: the backward and forward parts cancel. Distance counts both.

questions.prompt: The region under y = √x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the solid?
questions.explanation: Discs with radius √x: V = π∫₀⁴ (√x)² dx = π∫₀⁴ x dx = 8π.
choiceExplanations: 16π forgets the 1/2 in the antiderivative x²/2.
8 forgets the factor π in the disc area πR².
16π/3 uses √x as the area of the disc. The radius must be squared.

questions.prompt: Water flows into a tank at r(t) = 4t liters per minute. The tank holds 10 liters at t = 0. How much water is in the tank at t = 3 minutes?
choiceExplanations: 46 uses 4t² as the antiderivative of 4t. It is 2t².
22 adds the rate at t = 3 (12) to the starting amount. Add the integral of the rate.
18 is the water added. Add the 10 liters that were already there.

questions.prompt: The region between y = x and y = x² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the solid?
questions.explanation: Washers with outer radius x and inner radius x²: V = π∫₀¹ (x² − x⁴) dx = π(1/3 − 1/5) = 2π/15.
choiceExplanations: π/6 does not square the radii: π∫(x − x²) dx.
8π/15 adds the squares instead of subtracting the inner one.
π/30 squares the difference, π∫(x − x²)² dx. Washers subtract the squares instead.

questions.prompt: A solid's base is the region under y = √x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. Cross-sections perpendicular to the x-axis are squares. What is the volume?
questions.explanation: Each square has side √x, so area (√x)² = x. V = ∫₀⁴ x dx = 8.
choiceExplanations: π comes from semicircle cross-sections, (π/8)∫₀⁴ x dx = π. These are squares.
8π is the volume of revolution about the x-axis (discs). Square cross-sections have no π.
16/3 integrates the side length √x instead of the square's area.
